The area is a city radius; no page gives the land held in exile. Ewe and Aja states are said to be tributary 'by the end of the 16th century' (tributary tint, not drawn).

6,032 km2 round Oyo-Ile (4.2-5.2 E, 7.9-8.8 N): Ofinran 'regained Oyo's original territory from the Nupe', Abipa repopulated Oyo-Ile (his cults date to the early 17th century), and the infobox returns the capital to Oyo-Ile c. 1615, six years after the shape begins. Oyo failed to conquer Benin 'sometime between 1578 and 1608'.

29,176 km2: 'Oyo entered a long period of growth in the 17th century'. The infobox gives 150,000 km2 for 1680, a ratio of 0.19 to this shape; the same page has Oyo raiding southward only from 1682 and subjugating Dahomey in 1748, so the infobox figure looks too high for 1680 (it would suit the 18th-century peak, when the shape is 88,000 km2, ratio 0.59) and the shape is kept. [Reviewer af-04-a: confidence lowered from 3 to 2; the Oyo page dates the 1823 raid but gives no year for the defeat that ended the hegemony, and the Dahomey page has 1823 (infobox) against 1827 (text).] 'In 1823, Dahomey raided Oyo's protected villages. Peace talks broke down, Oyo attacked, and it was decisively defeated, ending its hegemony over Dahomey.' The Dahomey page has it at 1823 (infobox) and at Paonignan in 1827 (body text).

wars.name: Nupe conquest of Oyo
wars.outcome: The Nupe occupied Oyo about 1535, sacked the capital and drove the dynasty into exile in Borgu; Ofinran regained the land after about 80 years.
wars.note: The Sokoto Caliphate page dates the fall of the Nupe Kingdom itself to c. 1808.

wars.name: Oyo-Dahomey wars

wars.outcome: Both campaigns, in 1783 and 1789, failed; no territory moved.

wars.outcome: An Oyo-Dahomey-Lagos force blockaded Badagri; no territory moved.

wars.name: Ilorin secession and the Fulani war

zones.text: Ilorin and the north of Oyo

wars.outcome: Afonja refused Awole's order in 1793, forced Awole's suicide in 1795 and seceded Ilorin in 1817; Afonja was killed in 1823 and Ilorin joined the Sokoto Caliphate; Ilorin destroyed Oyo-Ile in 1835.
wars.note: The Ilorin Emirate page gives no year for Afonja's revolt or for the burning of Oyo-Ile and puts the alliance of Alimi and Afonja at about 1810; the Sokoto page says only that Ilorin 'backed by the Sokoto Caliphate, launched a series of attacks'.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW. 9 shapes 1609-1835. The 1300 start is the page's own estimate ('the founding is regarded as 1300 but only estimated'), so the two new keyframes before 1609 and the found event are low confidence. Corrections: Dahomey is removed from the 1752-1835 shapes because the Dahomey page makes it a tributary (1730 infobox, 1748 text, to 1823); the 1820 and 1834 shapes lose Oyo-Ile although it was the capital to 1835. Not resolved: the 1769 shape overlaps the Ashanti 1769 shape between 0.1 and 0.7 E and reaches the Volta coast and Danish Gold Coast (Cliopatria neighbour list) with no page behind it; the Ewe and Aja tributaries, the Egba, Egbado and Porto-Novo (the Dahomey page: Porto-Novo 'under Oyo protection') are inside the shape as direct land because no page dates when each paid tribute. AREA. Infobox 150,000 km2 in 1680 against the shape's 29,176 km2 (ratio 0.19); the peak shape is 87,978 km2 (0.59). The infobox looks too high for 1680. DISAGREEMENTS. Dahomey's vassalage 1730 (infobox) or 1748 (text); its release 1823 (infobox) or 1827 (Paonignan); Oyo-Igboho capital c. 1535-1615 (infobox) but built by Ofinran after the return (text). AFTER 1835. The Alaafin line continues at Ago d'Oyo (New Oyo) under Atiba (d. 1859); Cliopatria ends the row in 1835. New Oyo, Ibadan, the Egba (Abeokuta) and the Ilorin Emirate need dossiers; Ilorin 1817-1823 under Afonja was a rebel state in all but name and is left to the Sokoto group (af-03) or to a rebel dossier. RULERS. The Oyo page gives reign years only for Adelu (1859-1876) and Adeyemi I (1876-1905), so no ruler strip. PAGE BUDGET. Five pages opened (up to 5 allowed).
